chapter: Sidemen, the Hampton years, race and money
title: Paul Bley, Eric Dolphy and Ted Curson
summary: Mingus's judgments: Bley partial fit, Dolphy sincere, Curson not serious about music.

blocks.x: How about Paul Blay? I always liked him playing with you.
CERTAIN ELEMENTS OF (Inaudible) my music, he could play very well with it. But not all the way around. Horace Horace Parlan I liked better.
Horace was very, very good. How about Eric?
Eric was very sincere about learning the music, yeah. He was a very sincere person, I can say. Won't do anything unless he gets it right. How about Ted Curson? Curson?
No, man, he never played my music.
He was with you a long time.
I think he's playing (Inaudible) plays my music now, with his own band.
Did you ever hear his own band?
He sounded very good. He's -- surprisingly, though, the person I think of most directly when I hear Ted is Louis Armstrong.
I can't imagine him ever playing with that him. good
Because he's never serious about music.
Well, he was playing very well, very direct and very brassy. Very simple.
I never thought he swung, learned how to swing.
He was very tentative when he was playing with you. He always seemed to be jumpy, nervous, and not --
That's his personality. Not because he's playing with me. That's the way he plays. ed.
